correctness.rationale: PASS for the repaired package only. The frozen centralizer proof at line 43 incorrectly forbids merging across more than one boundary: for example the zero face below a rank-three chamber deletes all three cuts and certainly commutes. The replacement proof counts fibers over the actual common product, not hypothetical locally allowable merges. Compatible sign vectors have a coordinate-wise union, realizable by the face product. Any refinement gamma of alpha gives exactly 2^r commuting beta below gamma with product gamma, since beta must retain every cut missing from alpha and is free on alpha's r cuts. Refinements of alpha split its zero block by an arbitrary signed face and each nonzero magnitude block by an independent ordered partition with fixed signs. This proves the frozen centralizer formula, including rank 0. In the tuple formula, cuts of the common product must survive in nonempty position subsets, giving the stated weight; feeding the signed-block count into the EGF gives the stated denominator. Its nearest pole is the unique positive real pole, with negative derivative of the denominator −2^(t+1), giving the displayed asymptotic. Common signed suffixes index the same one-cut rays in two chambers; any subset of common rays gives one common subface. Every clique embeds in some chamber interval, and its chamber makes that interval maximal. No numerical formula was changed.
residual_risks: Small-rank reproduction does not certify the general proof. The corrected common-product argument supplies the all-rank result.
